column3: Close to the Hebrew.
“It was distress to Amnon to make himself sick” is rendered “Amnon was so frustrated … that he made himself ill.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Weak” is rendered “depressed,” and “in the morning in the morning” as “morning after morning.”
“Make yourself sick” is rendered “pretend to be ill.”
“Two cakes” is rendered “a couple of cakes.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Cooked” is rendered “baked.”
“Poured out before him” is rendered “dished them out before him.”
“The chamber” is rendered “the bedroom.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Humble me” is rendered “violate me,” and “disgraceful folly” as “disgraceful thing.”
“Where will I bring my reproach” is rendered “where could I get rid of my reproach.”
“Humbled her” is rendered “violated her.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew is difficult (“do not the causes of this great evil …”); NASB renders “No, because this wrong in sending me away is greater.” The meaning is uncertain.
“Send away” is rendered “throw … out.”
“A garment of palms and soles” (Hebrew כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים) is rendered “a long-sleeved garment”; the exact garment is uncertain.
“Went continuously and cried out” is rendered “went away, crying aloud as she went.”
“Set your heart to” is rendered “take … to heart,” and NASB adds “was” to “remained and was desolate.”
NASB follows the Hebrew, without the longer Septuagint wording; “it burned to him” is rendered “he was very angry.”
“Humbled” is rendered “violated.”
“Two years of days” is rendered “two full years,” and “shearers” as “sheepshearers.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Heavy on you” is rendered “burdensome to you.”
“And not” is rendered “If not.”
Close to the Hebrew; NASB supplies “he let … go.”
“Good of heart” is rendered “merry,” and “sons of strength” as “valiant.”
Close to the Hebrew.
